hooks.text: Mars hides a canyon that would stretch across America.
A Martian canyon drops seven kilometers deep into the crust.
The largest canyon in our solar system sits on Mars.

title: The Martian canyon that dwarfs the Grand Canyon
description: Discover Valles Marineris, a massive Martian rift system that stretches across an entire continent and plunges miles deep.

beats.text: Most people picture small rifts when they think of Martian valleys.
beats.visual: Noctis Labyrinthus fractured plateau landscape imaged by Mars Express HRSC, 2004

beats.text: NASA spacecraft revealed it spans up to four thousand kilometers long.
beats.visual: Mariner 9 spacecraft model on display at NASA, 1971

beats.text: Tectonic rifting ripped open the crust as nearby volcanic bulges surged.
beats.visual: Ius and Tithonium Chasmata perspective view from Mars Express HRSC, 2006

beats.text: Its sheer walls plunge seven kilometers deep into the planet.
beats.visual: Candor Chasma layered terrain imaged by Mars Global Surveyor MOC, 2003
queries: Candor Chasma Mars Global Surveyor MOC

beats.text: Yet young volcanic cones sit quietly on the immense canyon floor.
beats.visual: Volcanic cones in Coprates Chasma imaged by Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, 2007

beats.text: An entire continent fits neatly inside this colossal Martian canyon.
beats.visual: Valles Marineris global mosaic from Mars Odyssey THEMIS, 2008
